original_question: What is the name of the condition associated with parastremmatic dwarfism that limits normal joint movement?

final_qi.question: What is the name of the condition associated with parastremmatic dwarfism that limits normal joint movement?
final_qi.long_answer: Parastremmatic dwarfism is a TRPV4-related skeletal dysplasia in which newborns frequently show multiple congenital joint contractures. These contractures restrict the normal range of motion and are collectively termed arthrogryposis (arthrogryposis multiplex congenita), the condition that limits normal joint movement in this disorder.

final_answer.long_answer: Parastremmatic dwarfism, better termed parastremmatic dysplasia, is an extremely rare autosomal-dominant skeletal dysplasia produced by gain-of-function mutations in the TRPV4 calcium-permeable channel gene. Affected individuals show profound short stature, severe limb bowing, scoliosis, joint contractures, and distinctive radiographic changes such as marked platyspondyly and irregular metaphyseal ossification. Thus, it is a specific genetic disorder of bone development rather than a general form of short stature.

final_answer.long_answer: Parastremmatic dwarfism is a TRPV4-related skeletal dysplasia in which newborns frequently show multiple congenital joint contractures. These contractures restrict the normal range of motion and are collectively termed arthrogryposis (arthrogryposis multiplex congenita), the condition that limits normal joint movement in this disorder.
